source_review.notes: Checked official RFC Editor records for RFC 2330, 2678, 5136, 7679, 7680, 6390, 6703, 2544 and 9097. Current one-way delay and loss sources correctly replace RFC 2679 and 2680; document status is stated without treating Informational benchmarking methods as production guarantees.

evidence: Checked requirement tuple R=(S,D,P,W,F,M,theta,E) and directional S-to-D measurement semantics.
Checked Type-P, interval [T,T+I], Ns, Nr, Bu, O, C, U, G, one-way delay di, quantile Qp, loss L and availability notation.
Checked bit/s versus byte/s and decimal-unit declarations throughout calculations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Metric symbols identify observations and constraints, not causal attribution.

evidence: Recomputed replication goodput as 520.00 Mbit/s, p95 nearest rank over ten samples as 34 ms and loss as 0.040 percent.
Recomputed telemetry goodput as 7.20 Mbit/s, p95 as 121 ms and loss as 0.500 percent.
Recomputed 900 MB in 12 seconds as 600 Mbit/s and 700 Mbit/s offered on 1 Gbit/s as 70 percent utilization and 30 percent headroom.
Recomputed 100 losses among 200,000 as 0.05 percent.
Recomputed 1.8 TB over eight hours as 500 Mbit/s and 150 Mbit/s shortfall; recomputed Exercise 3 nearest-rank p50=15, p90=22 and p99=45 ms.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Quantile results explicitly use nearest-rank convention and small-sample limitations.

evidence: Checked G=8Bu/I, U=O/C, loss=(Ns-Nr)/Ns for positive Ns and di=tD,i-tS,i.
Checked nearest-rank selection ceil(p*n) and all examples against sorted samples.
Checked simultaneous offered-load feasibility as a necessary capacity bound, not a sufficient tail guarantee.
Checked capacity, available capacity, throughput and goodput remain distinct by layer and interval.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Equations are conditional measurement definitions and planning bounds, not universal performance laws.

evidence: Reviewed zero sent packets, zero received packets, duplicates, late arrival, corruption, reordering, fragmentation and capture loss.
Reviewed asymmetric paths, clock error, route changes, packet-size distributions, bursts, cross traffic, endpoint saturation and test-generator limits.
Reviewed required allows and denies, idle versus peak conditions, one-link/device/site/provider failures, degraded capacity, restoration and correlated failures.
Reviewed tele-stroke and emergency-call cases with clinical/public-safety, accessibility, privacy/legal, security, operations, regulatory and independent assurance roles.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-stakes authorization and jurisdiction-specific service obligations remain human-review requirements.

evidence: Checked every metric requires endpoint, direction, traffic type, layer, interval, units, statistic, threshold and method identity.
Checked delay and loss share a declared population and timeout accounting rule.
Checked representative offered load and operating/failure conditions accompany capacity and tail claims.
Checked network observations remain separated from endpoint, application and measurement-system limits.
Checked failure requirements name failed domains, recovery windows and degraded objectives.
invariant_checking.notes: Executable checks cover declared sample arithmetic only; no live path or topology is measured.

evidence: Reviewed each arithmetic example with unit conversion and population definitions.
Reviewed why ping evidence is traffic-type and time specific and why RTT/2 does not prove one-way delay.
Reviewed finite zero-loss samples as unable to prove zero population loss and random samples as unable to establish rare tails.
Confirmed benchmark success, redundancy inventory and nominal rate are never presented as proofs of production service behavior.
proof_review.notes: The chapter gives finite calculations and necessary-condition arguments, not a proof of network fitness.

evidence: Audited uses of prove, reachable, capacity, available, reliable, lossless, guarantee, availability, sufficient and certify.
All metric claims carry scope and method; standards status is accurate; benchmark and synthetic evidence limits are explicit.
No external academic, practitioner, clinical, public-safety or regulatory review is claimed.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: High-consequence acceptance language is reserved for named authorized reviewers.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/NET-001/report.json
Reproduced exact goodput, nearest-rank p95, loss and pass/fail output for both synthetic flows under recorded Python 3.
Confirmed one of two flows passes the conjunction of declared thresholds.
Confirmed execution excludes traffic generation, route discovery, clock validation, population estimation, availability, policy authorization and real failure behavior.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution validates deterministic sample arithmetic only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter frames network quality as a vector of directional, workload-bound metric tuples and cleanly separates reachability policy, nominal capacity, available capacity, throughput, goodput, delay, variation, loss and availability while preserving later modules' mechanism depth.

practitioner_review.notes: Operational guidance covers traffic matrices, positive and negative reachability, normal and degraded targets, representative active/passive evidence, clock and tool limitations, endpoint confounders, raw evidence retention, failure exercises, restoration and attribution discipline.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten distinct examples and five exercises progressing from reachability and units through capacity, quantiles, loss, diagnosis, resilience and high-stakes public-service review. The executable evaluator reinforces conjunction and evidence boundaries.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
